xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax - TDS
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak:
The Company has received an order under Section 271C of the Income Tax Act, 1961 from the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax – TDS, dated 18-09-2025.
As per the order, the penalty imposed equals the shortfall in TDS deduction, which amounts to ₹1,85,260.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: It was alleged that the Company had failed to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on professional services, which were subject to TDS under Section 194J of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Accordingly, a Show Cause Notice was issued on 29.08.2025, providing an opportunity to the Company to explain why a penalty should not be imposed for failure to deduct tax at source under Section 194J.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: As per the order, the penalty imposed equals the shortfall in TDS deduction, which amounts to ₹1,85,260.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: DGGI, DZU GST issued show cause notice alleged that the Company availed and utilised ineligible Input Tax Credit (ITC) on invoices issued by it during the Financial Years 2018-19 and 2019-20. The Company is set to present its defence before the Additional Commissioner/ Joint Commissioner of Jaipur GST Commissionerate and is confident that pursuant to its submissions against the allegations in the Show Cause Notice, there will be no financial liability.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr:
The Company had filed an appeal before the Additional Commissioner, CGST, Jaipur. The adjudicating authority, after detailed examination, concluded that the Company was found to have complied with all applicable provisions under Section 16 of the CGST Act, 2017, supported by valid documentation including tax invoices, work orders, and banking records. Accordingly, the entire demand including tax, interest, and penalties has been dropped, and the amounts now stand at nil.
This was confirmed from the Order-in-Original received by the Company on 13-10-2025. The Company has also duly intimated the Stock Exchange of this development within the prescribed timeline.
With this, the matter now stands concluded.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Show Cause notice issued for income chargeable to tax has escaped assessment within the meaning of section 147 of the Act for Assessment Year 2019-20. Accordingly, notice to show cause as to why a notice under section 148 of the income Tax Act, 1961 should not be issued. Following a thorough evaluation Based on the prevailing law, legal advice and Company’s judgement, the company has responded to the Income Tax Act authorities and determined that this matter carries no financial implications on the Company and is hopeful that no financial liability will arise from the proceedings.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has received a Court Order on October 17, 2025, in the matter. As per the said Order, the Hon’ble Court has set aside the impugned Notice issued under Section 148 and all other proceedings / orders emanating therefrom.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Deputy Commissioner, State tax, GST department
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Adjudication cum demand order issued for availing and utilising ineligible ITC (relating to IPO expenses) during the Financial Year 2023-24. Accordingly, notice under section 74 of Rajasthan GST Act, read with similar sections of CGST Act 2017, to pay the tax determined, which has not been paid, and/or the Input Tax Credit (ITC) determined, which has been wrongfully availed and utilized along with interest under section 50 the said Act and penalty under Section 74 of the said Act."
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: Company has filed an appeal to appellate authorities and decision is pending.
